title: Embeddings cost blitz — quick compare
summary: One-week exploratory spreadsheet to compare unit cost and latency of various embedding models and batch configurations. Goal: identify cheap/fast configs for bulk vectorization and interactive search. Not final — next steps: run 10k query sample, confirm throughput on Dedicated pools.
rows: E1, redwood-embed-base, fp16, 1, 64, 8.2, 210, $0.60, high recall, steady latency on small docs, Maya Chen, in_progress
E2, sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, fp16, 8, 128, 45.1, 95, $0.12, excellent throughput with batching, recall slightly lower on long docs, Priya Nair, review
E3, openclip/embedding-small, int8, 64, 64, 120.3, 260, $0.04, cheapest per-1k but p95 high for single-doc interactive; good for bulk offline, Diego Alvarez, draft
E4, onnx-quant-embed-8bit, int8, 16, 256, 52.0, 140, $0.03, tiny memory, needs warmup; observed spikes on cold start, Samir Patel, in_progress
E5, redwood-embed-large-v2, bf16, 1, 256, 3.9, 430, $1.20, best embedding quality (eval AUC), expensive — candidate for premium routes, Maya Chen, draft
E6, hosted-embed-std (hosted-api), managed-quant, 8, 128, 30.7, 110, $0.35, stable SLA, easier integration; compare cost vs Dedicated, Priya Nair, review
E7, custom-pruned-embed, int8, 32, 64, 67.5, 180, $0.02, promising cost but recall drop vs reference; needs eval suite, Diego Alvarez, draft
notes: quick checklist: sample 10k docs (mix short/long), run both bulk and single-doc workloads
interactive use-case target: p95 < 150ms for batch_size <= 8
bulk vectorization target: maximize throughput while keeping cost_per_1k < $0.06
observed: batching dramatically improves throughput for smaller models — record cold vs warm start numbers
open question: how much quantization degrades recall on our eval set? (run A/B with eval harness)
keep a column for memory footprint on 16GB GPU — decide Dedicated pool fit
